title: CSV Matches The Ledger
description: Finance doesn't spot-check one column of the export — they reconcile the whole thing against the books. Prove every single field of every single exported row matches the database exactly, not just the ones that are easy to eyeball.
successCondition: Book 5 shipments with deliberately varied data (different weights, prices, statuses via /advance, and at least one origin/destination label containing a comma). GET /api/tracking/export.csv and parse it (respecting CSV quoting for the comma-containing label). For each of the 5 shipments, querying the shipments table directly via `npm run db:psql` confirms every one of id, status, originLabel, destinationLabel, weightKg, distanceKm, priceCents, currency, and createdAt in the CSV row matches the corresponding DB column exactly — including that the comma-containing label round-trips through the CSV without getting truncated or misparsed into two columns.
hints: A correct CSV parser (not a naive split(',')) is required to handle the comma-containing origin/destination label correctly — that's deliberately part of what this challenge is testing.
Match rows between the CSV and the DB by id, since export order and DB query order aren't guaranteed to be identical.
